Why isn't expropriation of unowned or commonly owned property a crime on par with expropriation of privately owned property?

Expropriation of commonly owned property IS a crime on par with expropriation of privately owned property, and should be treated as such.

By definition, expropriation means, "taking property away from its owner(s)". So you can't expropriate unowned things; only appropriate ("take possession of") them. Appropriation of formerly unowned goods is a requirement for human life on earth. We must take control of, and make use of, resources from the world around us in order to survive. Even hunter-gatherers take possession of the meat and fruits that they collect, and farming societies have to take possession of land on which to grow their crops.
